overall_summary: FACTVERSE's audience is highly receptive to extreme space anomalies, exoplanet mysteries, and mind-bending cosmic comparisons, while psychological facts and basic animal trivia consistently underperform. Leveraging high-concept cosmic 'what-if' scenarios and extreme planetary weather yields the highest views and engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,023 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) represent the channel's peak performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme planetary conditions, using highly visual and evocative materials (e.g., rubies, burning ice, dark coal) in the titles and hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Saturn's Rings' (274 views) and 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (264 views) outperform standard trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Create comparison videos that pit well-known biological entities against massive cosmic or geological timelines to break the viewer's intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views across multiple uploads) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out standard psychological advice and brain trivia, as the audience is seeking grander, more cinematic mysteries.

next_video.concept: The Planet with Three Suns Where Night Never Falls
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a visual of three blazing suns in a single sky: 'Imagine living on a world where the sun never sets, and you have three different shadows.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that if you stood in the center, the chaotic gravitational pull of the three stars would slowly tear your body apart before you ever saw a sunset.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the high-performing space anomaly niche, using strong visual imagery (three suns, three shadows) and a deadly physical twist to maximize retention.

experiment: Test a 'What If' cinematic micro-story format where the viewer is the protagonist exploring a real, terrifying exoplanet (e.g., HD 189733b) to combine the space niche with horror/mystery storytelling.
